name: Artillery
what_it_is: Artillery is a cloud-native open-source load and performance testing platform installable via npm. It supports a wide range of application protocols and can scale tests out to AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, or Azure ACI without requiring DevOps infrastructure setup.
components: artillery CLI (packages/artillery) — orchestrates test execution and cloud dispatch
artillery-engine-playwright — load tests using real headless Chromium browsers
artillery-plugin-expect — adds HTTP response assertions for functional/acceptance testing
artillery-plugin-ensure — SLO/threshold checks that exit non-zero in CI/CD on failure
artillery-plugin-publish-metrics — exports metrics to Datadog, New Relic, CloudWatch, Dynatrace, Prometheus, Honeycomb, Splunk, and any OTel-compatible backend
artillery-plugin-fake-data — generates synthetic payload data for virtual users
artillery-plugin-apdex — computes and reports Apdex scores
@artilleryio/int-core — shared runner, phase scheduler, and built-in HTTP/WebSocket/Socket.io engines
measurement: Response latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99, p999)
Virtual user counts (active, created, completed, failed)
Custom metric publishing to Datadog, New Relic, CloudWatch, Prometheus, Honeycomb, Dynatrace, Splunk, and OTel-compatible backends
configuration: YAML test scripts defining config (target, phases, plugins, environments) and scenarios (flows, requests, think-time)
--target / -t flag to override the base URL at runtime
--environment / -e flag to select named environment blocks from config.environments
--variables / -v flag to inject a JSON object of variables into virtual users
--overrides flag to dynamically replace any value in the test script with a JSON patch
--dotenv / --env-file flag to load environment variables from a .env file
--payload / -p flag to supply a CSV file for data-driven virtual user payloads
--count flag to set number of workers (defaults to 1; locally defaults to CPU count in distribute mode)
--platform flag selects runtime: local (default), aws:lambda, az:aci
Multiple input scripts with -i flags for composable test definitions
modes: local — runs test workers on the local machine using available CPUs (distribute mode)
aws:lambda — distributed cloud execution on AWS Lambda (multiply mode, scales out workers)
aws:ecs (Fargate) — distributed cloud execution on AWS Fargate containers
az:aci — distributed cloud execution on Azure Container Instances
solo (-s) — creates a single virtual user for debugging/smoke-testing
constraints: No docker-compose file is provided; the official Dockerfile (node:22-bookworm-slim base) must be built manually — there is no pre-baked multi-service compose setup.
Azure Fargate and ACI platforms are licensed under BSL, not MPL 2.0; commercial/production use on Azure requires a paid license.
gRPC and Kinesis engines are not bundled in @artilleryio/int-core — they require separate community or third-party engine packages (e.g., artillery-engine-grpc) to be installed alongside artillery.
Playwright browser load testing requires Chromium to be installed via `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`; the base Docker image pre-installs this but it adds significant image size.
Distributed cloud runs require AWS credentials (IAM, S3, SQS, Lambda/ECS/SSM) or Azure credentials to be available in the execution environment.
The --count flag's distribute mode is local-only; cloud platforms always use multiply mode, which replicates the full scenario load per worker rather than splitting it.
docker_services: artillery (single-service) — node:22-bookworm-slim image running the artillery CLI binary; no compose file; built from packages/artillery/Dockerfile
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml anywhere in the repository
No built-in fault/chaos injection (latency injection, error rate forcing, network partition simulation)
No built-in dashboard UI — metrics visualisation requires external tools (Grafana + Prometheus dashboard JSONs provided as examples only)
No native TCP or UDP protocol engines
No built-in distributed tracing / correlation ID injection
